events.credibility_reason: Several F10 signals together: six years with no referee, citation, or expert engagement on what would be a landmark result; the Erdős problems database (updated Aug 2025) and Wikipedia (Sep 2026) still treat the question as open and do not mention the claim; twelve revisions, with the proof's architecture changing (a CoP route added) while the claim stayed the same; the key lemma is cited, not proved; the second route is conditional; the author's same framework drew a note that reviewers did not understand it; and the claim conflicts with the stable numerical density near 0.074.
v3 'Major correction' concedes that earlier complexity, absoluteness and completeness claims were overstated.
The author calls it conjectural; an AI check flagged issues the author accepted; no human reading; the write-up itself is unread.

why: Only Agama's preprint claims to answer the question. Its first argument dates to July 2020, and v12 (March 2026) says the ideas are unchanged, so it falls before the snapshot. I marked it not_credible: there has been no uptake in six years on a landmark question, later authorities still list the problem as open, the proof architecture shifted across many revisions, and the key lemma is cited rather than proved. Hinman et al. give an upper bound on density, which cannot decide positivity, so it is a bound. Gibbs–McCranie is a finite computation, so it is instances. Ulam words are a different object, so that event is a variant. The Clement–Steinerberger and Gilson results concern growth, gaps and logical complexity, so they are none. Chojecki's 2026 notes assume positive upper density, which is the hypothesis at issue, so they settle nothing (none). By the poster's own account GPT produced their content, so they are marked generated, but they are set aside anyway. MalekZ's posts state no result, and AlphaProof Nexus shows only an attempt.
doubts: The Chojecki PDFs were never read; their ai_role rests on forum quotes. If a specialist ever confirms Agama's Section 5, the pre-snapshot whole would make the problem open_stale.
